text:
maria: Heads up — after the infra upgrade yesterday I’m seeing a 12-18% tail latency regression for short seq (<=32) requests on h100 pools. Root cause looks like the kernel selector now prefers an fp16 fused-kernel path that’s slower at small seqlen.

josh: Can you paste profiler output? did driver or cuda change? :thinking_face: 

maria: Yep, CUDA 12.3 -> 12.4 and kernel driver 540.x -> 550.x on the nodes that regressed. Here’s the perf snippet from last 10k tokens: 

```
profile: kernel_choice_histogram
model: gpt-medium-q4
arch: h100
seq=16 -> kernel: fused_attn_v2 (avg 1.8ms)
seq=64 -> kernel: sparse_attn_opt (avg 2.4ms)
seq=256 -> kernel: large_block (avg 8.1ms)
previously (CUDA12.3): seq=16 -> kernel: tiled_attn_fast (avg 1.1ms)
```

maria: The selector now maps seq_bin<=32 to fused_attn_v2 on H100 after autotune pass. That is slower in practice for our batch shapes.

samir: Oof. Possible causes: autotuner sampled different micro-benchmarks after driver change, or kernel performance shifted due to kernel launch overhead changes.

sylvie: We should check autotuner sampling artifacts and the cache that stores kernel picks. Do we persist per-host/driver picks?

maria: Yes, we persist a JSON in /var/lib/redwood/kernel-autotune/{model_sig}.json keyed by model+arch+driver+quant. But it only stores the single best kernel per seq_bin, and we don’t version it by autotune-commit or keep historical metrics.

josh: That persistence design is risky — driver/cuda upgrades can change absolute ordering. We need a more defensive cache schema.

kevin: Idea: include a hardware+driver fingerprint and autotune-run-id in the stored signature, and record the sampled metrics (p50,p95,p99,stderr,count) for each kernel. That way we can detect shifts and avoid blindly trusting a stale choice.

samir: Also consider storing a small fallback score delta and a last-sampled timestamp. Then on startup, if driver version changes or timestamp older than X, mark seq_bins as "stale" and trigger a fast-local-sample for top-2 candidates.

maria: Agreed. Example sig we could use: 
```
model_sig = f"{model}:{arch}:{cuda_version}:{driver_version}:{quant}:{autotune_commit}"
```
We also should add `seq_bin` to key.

sylvie: For the fast-local-sample, run N=5 micro-runs with real batch shapes and measure mean+std. If delta > 10% vs persisted pick, switch and write new record. Keep this cheap (<50ms per seq_bin).

josh: We also need invalidation when runtime/driver upgrades occur cluster-wide. infra-bot could broadcast a "driver-upgrade" event with affected nodes. The selector can set a per-node tombstone so we don’t use node-local cache entries that were collected on old drivers.

infra-bot: deploy-note: driver upgrade started on pool-h100-1..4 at 2025-11-21T03:12Z. Tags: cuda=12.4 driver=550.3. Will post completion.

maria: Another wrinkle: model reloads often change sequence-length distribution. Our autotune uses uniform seq sampling; we should weight sampling by observed seqlen hist for that model (collected over last 24h) so the chosen kernel optimizes for real traffic.

samir: Right — kernel utility = weighted_mean(latency, seqlen_hist). We can compute a cost function token_cost = latency * (seq/avg_seq) to bias smaller seq bins correctly.

kevin: Regarding cache invalidation semantics: plan:
- persistent store keeps entries per (model_sig, seq_bin) with metrics and autotune_run_id
- if CUDA/driver/arch changes -> mark entries STALE (do not delete)
- on first request for seq_bin with STALE -> run fast-local-sample and update entry atomically
- provide admin endpoint to force full re-autotune per model

josh: We should also record which kernel variants are compatible with fallback (i.e., semantic compatibility). Then the smart router can fallback to a compatible variant if chosen kernel misses at runtime.

maria: We saw that earlier today: fused_attn_v2 fails for certain quantized models (nan) but selector had no compatibility metadata so it was used and then we fell back to CPU path which killed latency. Need compatibility mask in DB.

sylvie: For compatibility, add schema fields: supports_q4, supports_kv_cache, needs_padding_patch. Those are boolean flags discovered at autotune time.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: 2025-11-21T08:17Z pool-h100-3 avg P99 increased 15% for gpt-medium-q4 short_seq. Trace id: pr-20251121-8912

maria: I pushed a quick fix to the selector: prefer tiled_attn_fast for seq<=32 on H100 if stored metric delta > 0.08. Canary on pool-h100-2 for 2h.

samir: Thanks. Post-mortem action items:
1) Revise persist schema to include driver/cuda fingerprint and autotune-run-id
2) Implement fast-local-sample on STALE entries and on node-join after driver change
3) Weight autotune sampling by observed seq distribution per model
4) Record compatibility metadata for kernel variants
5) Add canary infra for kernel-selector changes and perf-bot gating

josh: I’ll own 1+2. samir take 3, sylvie take 4, maria run the canary and 5.

kevin: One more: record a lightweight bloom filter of successful kernel runs per model to quickly check whether a kernel historically worked for that model+quant without querying full DB. Helps avoid bad picks.

maria: Thanks all — will follow up with PR for selector changes and a small design doc for the persistent schema. Posting links here when ready. :rocket:
